extraction.name: VAP-Data
extraction.description: A semantic-controlled paired dataset for video generation with over 100K curated paired samples across 100 semantic conditions, covering four primary categories: concept, style, motion, and camera.
extraction.creator: Yuxuan Bian, Xin Chen, Zenan Li, Tiancheng Zhi, Shen Sang, Linjie Luo, Qiang Xu
extraction.citeAs: Bian, Yuxuan; Chen, Xin; Li, Zenan; Zhi, Tiancheng; Sang, Shen; Luo, Linjie; Xu, Qiang. Video-As-Prompt: Unified Semantic Control for Video Generation. arXiv:2510.20888v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was bootstrapped by curating thousands of high-quality real reference images from the Internet, spanning men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases, and then using Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs to create paired videos by matching each image to all compatible templates. The resulting dataset contains over 100K paired videos across 100 semantic conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 2K high-quality reference images collected from the Internet, plus Image-to-Video visual-effects templates from commercial models (VIDU and Kling) and community LoRAs used to generate paired videos.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors created paired videos by matching each curated reference image to all compatible visual-effects templates, noting that some templates restrict subject categories. VAP-Data was created using visual effects templates from commercial models and community LoRAs, making the dataset synthetic and derived from other generative models.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors curated high-quality reference images and matched each image to compatible templates. For evaluation, they evenly sampled 24 semantic conditions from 4 categories in the test subset, with 2 samples each, totaling 48 test samples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 randomly selected video-generation researchers participated in the user study.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the authors construct and release VAP-Data and that any artifact release will be accompanied by a research-only license and an acceptable-use policy prohibiting abusive or unlawful scenarios.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected reference images span men, women, children, animals, objects, landscapes, and multi-subject cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses misuse risks including identity impersonation, deepfake content, targeted harassment, deceptive political messaging, and generation of sexualized or violent media. It states the system is intended for research, education, and creative prototyping, not for surveillance, impersonation, political persuasion, or other high-risk deployments, and mentions mitigations including a research-only release and default content filters blocking clearly harmful categories.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Because VAP-Data was created using visual effects templates from commercial models and community LoRAs, the dataset is synthetic and derived from other generative models, which may cause VAP to inherit specific stylistic biases, artifacts, and conceptual limitations of the source templates.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The semantic conditions in VAP-Data are relatively limited, synthetic, and derived from other generative models. The dataset may inherit source-template biases and artifacts. The paper notes that inaccurate semantic descriptions or large subject mismatch can degrade generation quality, multiple reference videos can blend unwanted visual details, and the approach adds extra inference cost in memory and runtime.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used to train and evaluate a unified semantic-controlled video generation model. The paper states intended uses are research, education, and creative prototyping. For evaluation, a test subset was formed by evenly sampling 24 semantic conditions from 4 categories with 2 samples each.
